9ebc0b77 chore: release (#382)
200:## Wire-format fixtures
201-
202-A wire-format fixture is a file or test script that stands in for the bytes a provider sends. A reader must know which bytes are real and which bytes are not. Five rules apply.
203-
204-SMA-585 shows the risk. `responses_tool_call.txt` is a CAPTURED fixture, but the file ended with a `[DONE]` line that the Responses endpoint does not send. The header did not record the line.
205-
206-1. **Label.** Each fixture states its provenance. Use one of three labels: CAPTURED (name the endpoint, the model and the date), HAND-AUTHORED, or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts.
207-2. **Edits.** A CAPTURED fixture lists every edit from the raw capture in three parts: Removed, Added and Changed. Changed covers reorders, reformats and value edits. Write "nothing" for an empty part. The header of `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt` is the worked example.
208-3. **Hand-authored shapes.** A HAND-AUTHORED fixture names the source of each shape. The source is a capture or a vendored type. Do not copy framing from a different endpoint or API.
209-4. **No conformity edits.** Do not add, remove or reorder a line to make a fixture match a sibling fixture. If you must, record the edit under Changed.
210-5. **Where the header goes.** An SSE fixture or other text fixture carries a `:` comment header. A format with no comment syntax records its provenance in the doc comment of the test that loads it. An inline wire helper in test code cites its source in the same way. A synthetic addition in a test script is allowed if its doc comment says that it is not captured. The Gemini `done()` in `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs` is an example.
211-
212-## Documentation site
213-
214-The public docs site is built from `docs/book/`.
215-
216-```bash
217-cargo install mdbook --version 0.4.43 --locked
218-cargo install mdbook-linkcheck --version 0.7.7 --locked
219-cd docs/book && mdbook serve
220-```
221-
222-`mdbook serve` opens `http://localhost:3000` with live-reload. The CI `book-build` job runs `mdbook build`, which includes linkcheck because the `[output.linkcheck]` backend is declared in `book.toml`; broken internal links fail the build.
223-
224-Deployment to GitHub Pages happens automatically on push to `main` via `.github/workflows/docs.yml`. The repo's Pages source is configured as **GitHub Actions** (Settings → Pages); future contributors do not need to touch this setting unless the workflow's deploy strategy changes.
225-
226-The `mdbook build` output lands under `docs/book/book/html/` (because the `[output.linkcheck]` backend reorganizes the output tree). This path is only relevant for CI artifact uploads — `mdbook serve` reads from its own in-memory tree.
227-
228-In `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` specifically, tag prose snippets ` ```text `
229-or ` ```ignore ` — never a bare ` ```rust `. That file is `include_str!`'d into the
230-facade's rustdoc, so a `rust` fence becomes a doctest that CI's test gate will run.
231-
232-## Local pre-PR checklist
233-
234-Run these before pushing — they are the same gates CI runs:
235-
236-```bash
237-cargo fmt --all -- --check
238-cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
239-cargo test --workspace --all-features
240-RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
241-DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=80 NIGHTLY_CHANNEL=nightly-2026-05-01 \
242-  bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh
243-npm ci                                               # once, or after package-lock.json changes
244-npx markdownlint-cli2                                # reads .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc
245-bash scripts/check-markdownlint-config.sh            # asserts that config is in force
246-bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh         # cargo-visible workflow env is uniform
247-bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh # …and its parser still parses (fmt runs both)
248-bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh            # release gap report + release-plz.yml guards (fmt runs it)
249-bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade-selftest.sh      # the cascade guard keeps its rule (fmt runs it)
250-bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh                 # breaking bump needs breaking dependents (PR only; fmt runs it)
251-```
252-
253-The Markdown gate needs Node (>= 22); everything else in that list needs only the
254-Rust toolchain — except `check-doc-coverage.sh` and `check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh`,
255-which both use `mapfile` and so need bash >= 4.0. macOS ships bash 3.2, on which
256-they fail with `mapfile: command not found`; `brew install bash` alongside the
257-Rust toolchain is the fix.
258-`markdownlint-cli2` is pinned exactly in `package-lock.json` and is
259-**not** tracked by Dependabot — bumping it is a deliberate act, like
260-`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN`. `npx markdownlint-cli2 --fix` resolves most findings

The rule says that each fixture states its provenance: CAPTURED, HAND-AUTHORED, or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts. A CAPTURED fixture lists every edit from the raw capture in three parts: Removed, Added and Changed. A part with no edits says "nothing".

<issue id="e87dea71-f32a-4ffd-aafb-27e38eec8e87" label="SMA-585" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-585/responses-tool-calltxt-carries-a-trailing-data-done-its-provenance" /> makes the OpenAI Responses fixtures follow the rule. Fixtures in other crates do not follow it yet.

* LiteLLM CAPTURED fixtures: for example, `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/fixtures/tool_call_stream.txt` lines 1-9 name the capture but list no edits.
* `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_text_usage_trailing.txt` is part captured (LiteLLM proxy) and part reconstructed. It also shortens the response id. Under the rule, its label must name the reconstructed parts, and the shortened id goes under Changed.
* `chat_text_usage_trailing_empty_choices.txt` is HAND-AUTHORED. Its header must name the source of each shape.
* Fixture directories with no provenance headers at all: `providers-anthropic` (9 files), `providers-gemini` (1), `cli` (4), `tools` (3, JSON, so the provenance goes in the doc comment of the test that loads them).

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

Before you start implementing, you must, in order:

1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
   human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
3. Get their approval of that doc.
4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.

If nothing is open when you write your first message and there's one
sensible way, steps 1 to 3 happen in that message (see Your First
Message).

Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
the questions.

## Look Before You Ask

In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
project or their context already answers, or reopen what they've
already decided.

## Your First Message

Move the work forward, with one of these:

- **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
  request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
  request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
  shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
  Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
  and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
  have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
  has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
  so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
  want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
  corrections. Then, if they haven't told you why they want it, even if
  you can guess, ask about that: one open question in their own terms,
  with nothing to pick from. If they have told you, and their request
  and the project leave open something whose answer would change what
  gets built, ask about the one that would change it most; when its
  choices can be named, sketch each concretely, with what it trades off
  and which you'd pick. If nothing like that is open, there's one
  sensible way: end with the short design itself (the approach, a line on
  why the others don't fit, and the design in a few lines) and ask them
  to approve it. Their approval covers the approach and the design: write
  the short design doc as approved and go on to the plan.
  Specs are often incomplete, so confirm before you build on one.
- **They haven't:** one open question, in their own terms, about the
  biggest thing their request leaves unsettled. Say why you're asking:
  what the answer would change about what you build. For "a website for
  my bakery": "If it's mostly for people deciding whether to stop by,
  I'd lead with hours and what's in the case today; taking orders is a
  different site. What do you want someone to do when they land on it?"

How the message ends depends on whether their message asked for
brainstorming:

- **They asked for it** (by name, by invoking it, or by asking for a
  design discussion): end there. They want this conversation.
- **They didn't:** they may not want a conversation at all. End with a
  light, one-line offer to just get going instead, like
  "Or if you'd rather I just dive in, say so." If they take you up on
  it, this skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
  (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
  asked through the normal workflow.

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Ask a question only when the answer would change what gets built and
neither the request nor the project answers it. Otherwise, state your
call and your reason as a proposal they can correct, and move the work
forward. Process steps are always your calls: writing things up, where
files go, looking further, how to show something. Do them and say so.
Ask one at a time. Use plain language, pitched just a little above where
your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use process jargon.
You never need to quote this skill to your human partner.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Until you know why they want it, ask open
questions, with no example answers attached. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Once you know why, when a decision has
choices you can name, sketch each concretely, with what it trades off
and which you'd pick. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?",
propose something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Read from how they
talk which of those choices they want to make. Someone who raises the how
or asks about trade-offs wants the options with your pick. Someone who
talks about outcomes is handing you the how: make those calls and state
each in a line. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Make every question specific** to their project and what they've told
you. Ask Socratically, the way a sharp colleague would: build each
question on their last answer or on something you found, so it helps
them think through a consequence or a case they may have missed
("Voting closes before the meeting, and two members joined this month.
Does someone who joins mid-round get a vote?"). When the reason isn't
already plain, say what you're hoping to learn or what the answer would
change. A proposal they can correct, plus your reason for it, often
beats a question.

**Do recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking further
would help, go look: deeper into their codebase or project, their own
files and data, or the web. Say what you looked for and what you found.

**Lay out the approaches.** Once you understand what they want, and
before you write anything up, put the ways of building it in a message
of its own. Come up with several real alternatives and drop the weak
ones, including any that work against why they want it and any the
existing work rules out. Sketch the two or three that remain concretely
enough to picture, grounded in what the project actually does, with what
each trades off. Recommend one and say why, then ask which way they want
to go; if they've handed you the how, say you'll go with your pick
instead. When there's genuinely one sensible way, say so in that
message and explain why the others don't fit; the design comes in the
next one. This is for how it gets built; for what they want, get them
describing first.

**Show, don't tell.** Whenever seeing would help more than reading,
sketch it in text: a few lines of what they'd see. Offer the visual
companion (below) when the look itself is theirs to decide:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Only what they said goes in as theirs. Anything you filled in goes in
as your proposal, with your reason. End each chunk by asking what's wrong
or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, put a
text sketch next to the description. If the look itself is theirs to
decide and they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the
offer instead (its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next
message. Once they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want and they've picked an approach, say
how big the work is in plain words. They can override it.

| Size | The design doc |
|------|----------------|
| A small change | a short one: what you already covered together, written down |
| A project | the full written design (below) |

Short or full, the design doc has an **Approaches** part: the two or
three ways you considered building it, what each trades off, which one
they picked, and why. They pick in the conversation, before you write
the doc.

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

Write a plain document a talented builder in the domain could plan
from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- approaches (above)
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

For a small change, the short design covers the same points in a line
or two each and goes straight to your human partner, without the
builder check.

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, pick a sensible place and say where. Your human partner's
preferences override both.

`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After the design doc is approved, the next step is the plan: invoke

</HARD-GATE>

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

You are a read-only forensic researcher. Work in /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-845 (a git worktree). STRICT RULES: do not edit, write, or create any file. Do not run any git command that moves HEAD or changes refs (no checkout, switch, reset, stash, rebase, merge, commit, branch, worktree). Read-only git is fine: git log, git show, git blame, git log -S/-G, git grep. `gh pr view <n> --json body,title` is fine. Work synchronously in the foreground.

Context: CONTRIBUTING.md section "Wire-format fixtures" (read it, lines ~200-211) requires every wire-format fixture to state its provenance: CAPTURED (endpoint, model, date + edits from raw capture in Removed/Added/Changed; write "nothing" for an empty part), HAND-AUTHORED (name the source of each shape: a capture or a vendored type), or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts. The worked example is the header of crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt — read it fully.

Your files:
- crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/fixtures/*.txt (6 files; two have CAPTURED headers without an edit list, four have no header)
- crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_*.txt (4 files; chat_text_usage_trailing.txt is part captured from a LiteLLM proxy and part reconstructed, with a shortened response id; chat_text_usage_trailing_empty_choices.txt, chat_content_filter.txt and chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt are HAND-AUTHORED)

For EACH file find, with evidence (commit SHA, PR number, design doc file:line under docs/superpowers/specs or plans, PR bodies via gh):
1. The commit/PR/SMA ticket that added it and every later change (git log --follow).
2. Captured or hand-authored, with evidence. If the record is silent say "no record"; do not guess. For the SMA-547 LiteLLM captures, read the SMA-547 design doc "Evidence" section and find any recorded raw capture to compare against.
3. For captured ones: endpoint, proxy/image, model, date, method, and every known edit from the raw capture (Removed/Added/Changed). E.g. does the fixture drop the ": " keepalive lines, `event:` lines, the [DONE] line, usage chunks, change ids, reformat JSON? Compare line by line against any raw trace in the repo or PR bodies.
4. For hand-authored ones: what each shape is modelled on (capture? async-openai vendored type? docs?). Check rule 3: no framing copied from a different endpoint. E.g. does a LiteLLM fixture end with [DONE] and does the LiteLLM proxy really send it?
5. Any line that the wire would not send.
6. How the tests load them (litellm tests/streaming.rs, openai tests/chat_streaming.rs, etc.) and whether adding a `:` comment header at the top is safe (does the SSE parser skip `:` comment lines? any byte or line counting?). Give file:line.

Report: a per-file table plus evidence lines. Mark each claim VERIFIED or INFERRED. Concise but complete.

input.prompt:
You are a read-only forensic researcher. Work in /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-845 (a git worktree). STRICT RULES: do not edit, write, or create any file. Do not run any git command that moves HEAD or changes refs (no checkout, switch, reset, stash, rebase, merge, commit, branch, worktree). Read-only git is fine (log, show, blame, log -S, grep). `gh pr view <n> --json body,title` is fine. Work synchronously in the foreground.

Context: CONTRIBUTING.md section "Wire-format fixtures" (read it, lines ~200-211). A wire-format fixture "is a file or test script that stands in for the bytes a provider sends". Each must state provenance: CAPTURED (endpoint, model/version, date, + edits in Removed/Added/Changed), HAND-AUTHORED (name the source of each shape: a capture or vendored type/docs), or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts. Rule 5: a text format with comment syntax carries the header in the file; a format with no comment syntax (JSON) records provenance in the doc comment of the test that loads it.

Your files:
- crates/paigasus-helikon-cli/tests/fixtures/agents.toml, tools/lookup_spending.rhai, triage_script.json, triage.jsonl
- crates/paigasus-helikon-tools/tests/fixtures/article.html, brave_search.json, tavily_search.json

Questions per file:
1. Is it a wire-format fixture at all under that definition (does it stand in for bytes a provider / external service sends), or is it a config / input / script fixture? Explain. For triage_script.json: is it a scripted model reply that mimics a provider wire shape, or the SDK's own internal type? Read how eval_cli.rs / mcp_cli.rs and the CLI source use it.
2. The commit/PR/SMA ticket that added it (git log --follow), and any design doc (docs/superpowers/specs|plans) evidence on where its shape came from (Brave Search API docs? a real capture? Tavily docs? vendored types?). If the record is silent say "no record".
3. Which test(s) load it (file:line) — the tools ones load from src/web/fetch.rs:356, src/web/backends/brave.rs:118,139, tavily.rs:125. Does that loading test already have a doc comment? For article.html: HTML has comment syntax <!-- -->; would adding an HTML comment change any test assertion (e.g. extracted-text equality, length)? For TOML/rhai/jsonl: comment syntax exists for TOML (#) and rhai (//); JSONL has none.
4. Any field in the JSON that the real API would not send, if you can tell from docs in the repo or the backend's deserialization structs.

Report a per-file table with the verdict (wire-format: yes/no), source, recommended header location, and evidence (file:line, SHA). Mark claims VERIFIED or INFERRED.

input.description: Audit conformance.rs inline helpers
input.prompt:
You are a read-only auditor. Work in /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-845 (a git worktree). STRICT RULES: do not edit, write, or create any file. Do not run any git command that moves HEAD or changes refs. Read-only git (log, show, blame, log -S) and `gh pr view --json body` are fine. Work synchronously in the foreground.

Context: CONTRIBUTING.md "Wire-format fixtures" (lines ~200-211). Rule 5: "An inline wire helper in test code cites its source in the same way [in its doc comment]. A synthetic addition in a test script is allowed if its doc comment says that it is not captured. The Gemini done() in tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs is an example." Each source must be labelled CAPTURED (endpoint/model/date + edits), HAND-AUTHORED (name the source of each shape), or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts.

Audit tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs (3300 lines). Modules: bedrock (~73), openai_chat (~592), litellm (~1123), anthropic (~1695), gemini (~2311, plus a doc block ~2225), openai_responses (~2858). For EACH frame-builder helper (message_start, text_delta, tool_use_start, finish_chunk, usage_chunk, done, tool_call_start, tool_call_name_fragment, tool_call_args, frame, completed, output_item_added, etc.) and each module-level doc comment, report:
1. Does the helper (or its module doc) cite its source today? Quote the citation, file:line.
2. If it cites: does the citation follow the rule (label + edits/shape sources)? What is missing?
3. If it does not: what is the most likely source, with evidence (module doc comments, git log -S on the helper, the PR/design doc that added it, matching fixtures in crates/*/tests/fixtures). If no record, say "no record".
4. Any synthetic addition (a frame the real wire does not send, e.g. a [DONE] on an endpoint that does not send one, or Bedrock event framing) that lacks a "not captured" note.
5. Whether a helper's shape is copied from a different endpoint (rule 3), e.g. the litellm module reusing openai_chat framing.

Also: is there a module-level convention in the file already (e.g. a "# Provenance" doc section near line 2434) that the other modules should copy? Describe it.

Report one table per module with helper | cites today? | gap | likely source + evidence. Mark claims VERIFIED or INFERRED. Concise.

input.description: Inventory inline wire bytes in tests
input.prompt:
Read-only search in /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-845. Do not edit files and do not run any git command that moves HEAD. Thoroughness: medium.

Goal: size a scope question. CONTRIBUTING.md "Wire-format fixtures" (lines ~200-211) says "An inline wire helper in test code cites its source" in its doc comment. I need to know how many inline wire-byte helpers/literals exist in test code OUTSIDE tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs and outside the tests/fixtures directories.

Search provider crates (crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-*/tests/*.rs and the #[cfg(test)] modules under crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-*/src/), plus crates/paigasus-helikon/tests/openai_litellm_message_parity.rs and crates/paigasus-helikon-tools/src/web (Brave/Tavily/fetch tests). Look for: functions that build SSE frames or provider response bodies (e.g. fn sse(...), fn frame(...), fn chunk(...), format!("data: {...}"), raw string literals with "data: {", JSON response bodies passed to wiremock set_body_json/set_body_raw that mimic a provider response, Bedrock event-stream frame builders).

For each file report: file path, count of distinct helper functions and count of standalone inline wire literals (approximate is fine), whether any of them already carry a provenance note (grep for Provenance|CAPTURED|HAND-AUTHORED|captured), and 1-2 example names with line numbers. Exclude request-body assertions (bytes we SEND) — only response bytes the provider sends count. Give a total at the end. Concise table.

content.text:
I have the facts I need. One new fact changes the order of the work:

- **SMA-840 is not merged.** It has 14 commits on a local branch in another worktree, with no push and no PR. Its captures (probe runs A and C, `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-sonnet-4-5`) will go into the same Anthropic fixture directory. If SMA-845 merges first, the Anthropic headers cite files that are not on `main`.
- The SMA-840 capture headers do not follow the rule either. For example, `: transcribed from the SMA-840 probe run A (claude-sonnet-5-5); signature replaced` has no Removed/Added/Changed parts. I will not touch that branch. I will tell you about it so that SMA-840 can fix it before it merges.

**Approaches**

1. **(My pick) One PR now, merged after SMA-840.** I do all the work now. I read the SMA-840 captures with read-only `git show`, which does not move the branch. Each Anthropic header names the comparison capture (SMA-840 probe run, model, date) and lists the fields that differ: no `ping`, no `signature` on the thinking start, no `container`/`stop_details`/`service_tier`, placeholder ids. The PR body says "merge after SMA-840", and I re-check the citations if the SMA-840 captures change before they merge. This has the smallest overhead. The cost is a merge-order dependency.
2. **Two PRs.** PR A covers everything except the Anthropic headers and merges now. PR B covers the Anthropic headers and starts after SMA-840 merges. There is no dependency, but there are two review loops.
3. **Wait for SMA-840.** This is simple, but all the work stops for a fixture group that is only one sixth of the scope.

**Two design calls in all three approaches (you can change them):**

- **"not recorded" instead of "nothing".** When no raw capture exists, I cannot show that a part is empty. Rule 2 does not cover this case. I propose to add one sentence to `CONTRIBUTING.md`: *"If the raw capture is not available, write 'not recorded' for a part you cannot check."* This changes the rule, so it is your decision.
- **Commits per crate**, with `test(providers)` and `docs(contributing)` types, so that release-plz gets no `feat` or `fix`. Fixture and test-file changes do go into packaged crate files, so each touched crate gets a patch bump and the facade cascade. I accept that.

Which approach do you want? Do you also accept the "not recorded" sentence?

:    `max_output_tokens`, `max_tool_calls`, `metadata`, `moderation`,

:    `safety_identifier`, `service_tier`, `store`, `temperature`, `text`,

:    `truncation`, and `user`. The same trimming happens one level deeper:
:    the raw capture's `usage.input_tokens_details` carries both
:    `cached_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`; this fixture keeps only
----

# SMA-845: wire-format fixture provenance audit

Linear: [SMA-845](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-845/audit-wire-format-fixture-headers-in-other-crates-against-the-new).
Rule: `CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format fixtures" (added by SMA-585, PR #381).

## Intent

SMA-585 added a provenance rule for wire-format fixtures and made the OpenAI
Responses fixtures obey it. The fixtures and wire helpers in the other crates
do not obey it yet. A reader of those files cannot tell which bytes a provider
really sent. This change makes each in-scope fixture and wire helper state its
provenance under the rule.

## Goals

1. Each in-scope fixture file carries a provenance header that obeys rules 1-5.
2. Each in-scope JSON fixture has its provenance in the doc comment of the test
   that loads it (rule 5).
3. Each in-scope inline wire helper cites its source in its doc comment (rule 5).
4. Each statement in a header is true to the record. Where the record is silent,
   the header says so.

## Non-goals

- No new captures. This work uses only the record that exists today.
- No change to translator or production code.
- No change to the `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests that feed `json!` values or typed
  chunks into a translator (for example `litellm/src/stream.rs`,
  `gemini/src/stream.rs`, `openai/src/backend/chat.rs`,
  `bedrock/src/stream.rs`). These do not serve bytes over HTTP. Sven chose
  this scope (option 2) on 2026-11-21.
- No change to the SMA-840 branch. Its capture headers also do not obey the
  rule. That is a finding for SMA-840, not work for this branch.
- No mdBook or crate README change. This is test-only and contributor-doc work
  with no effect on the public surface.

## Anti-goals

- A header that says "nothing" for a part that nobody can check. That is the
  defect SMA-585 found, in a new form.
- A header that names a source (a doc page, a capture) that the record does not
  show was used.
- A data edit made only to make a fixture look like a sibling (rule 4).

## Constraints

- **Header syntax.** SSE and `.txt` fixtures use `:` comment lines.
  `eventsource-stream` 0.2.3 ignores comment lines (`event_stream.rs:70`), and
  a following blank line dispatches nothing (`:100`). The Gemini
  `translate/mod.rs:355-358` loop skips lines that do not start with `data: `.
  The LiteLLM and OpenAI fixtures that already have a `:` header pass their
  tests today. So a `:` header is safe in each SSE fixture.
- **`tool_use_then_continuation.txt`.** `messages_streaming.rs:201-203`
  splits the file on `# --- turn 2 ---\n` and asserts two parts. The header
  goes at the top (into part 1) and must not contain that delimiter string.
- **`body_cut_inside_message_stop.txt`.** The file ends inside an event with no
  newline, on purpose. The header goes at the top. Do not touch the tail.
- **Line endings.** `.gitattributes` pins these fixture directories to
  `text eol=lf`. Do not change that.
- **Merge order.** The Anthropic headers cite the SMA-840 captures. SMA-840 is
  not merged (local branch
  `feature/sma-840-anthropic-provider-drops-thinking-signatures`, no PR on
  2026-11-21). This PR must merge after SMA-840. Before the merge, check the
  cited SMA-840 files again on `main`.
- **Commits.** Use `test(providers)`, `test(tools)`, `docs(contributing)` and
  `docs(specs)`/`docs(plan)`. No `feat` or `fix`. Each touched crate still gets
  a release-plz patch bump, because the changed files are in packaged crates.
  That is accepted.

## Approaches

1. **One PR now, merged after SMA-840 (chosen).** All work is done now. The
   SMA-840 captures are read with read-only `git show` on that branch. The PR
   body states the merge order. Cost: a merge-order dependency.
2. **Two PRs.** Everything except the Anthropic headers merges now. The
   Anthropic headers follow after SMA-840 merges. No dependency, but two review
   loops.
3. **Wait for SMA-840.** Simple, but it stops all the work for one fixture
   group.

Sven chose approach 1 on 2026-11-21.

## Decisions

### D1. Header form

Use the form of the worked example,
`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt`,
and of `responses_reasoning_then_text.txt` for a HAND-AUTHORED file. Keep the
header short when the record is short. A header contains, in this order:

1. `Provenance:` and one of the three labels.
   - CAPTURED: the endpoint (or proxy and image), the model, the date, and the
     ticket or PR.
   - HAND-AUTHORED: the ticket or PR, and the source of each shape.
   - CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts: the capture data, then a list of
     the parts that are reconstructed.
2. For a CAPTURED file: `Edits from the raw capture:` and the three parts
   Removed, Added and Changed.
3. Any line in the data that the wire did not send, with the reason.

### D2. "not recorded" (Claude's call, open for Sven at the spec gate)

When the raw capture is not in the repo, a header cannot show that a part is
empty. In that case the header writes `not recorded` for that part, with the
evidence that does exist. Add one sentence to rule 2 in `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

> If the raw capture is not available, write "not recorded" for a part that you
> cannot check, and say what evidence exists.

Sven did not answer this proposal when he chose approach 1. It stays in the
design as Claude's call until the spec gate.

### D3. Anthropic shapes: compare with the SMA-840 captures

Sven chose this on 2026-11-21. Each of the nine Anthropic fixtures is
HAND-AUTHORED. Its header names, for each event shape it uses, whether the
shape matches the SMA-840 capture and which fields differ.

- Comparison captures (on the SMA-840 branch, commit `9f3a84f3` on
  2026-11-21): `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt` (probe run A,
  `claude-sonnet-5-5`) and `thinking_text_tool_use.txt` (probe run C,
  `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`). Use only the files whose header says
  "transcribed from" a probe run. Do not use the SMA-840 files whose header
  says "synthetic".
- Known differences to check and record (from the research, to verify file by
  file):
  - The captures send a `ping` event. No SMA-317 fixture has one.
  - The capture `message_start` carries `container`, `stop_sequence`,
    `stop_details`, `cache_creation`, `service_tier`, `inference_geo`, `speed`
    and `diagnostics`. The fixtures do not. The fixture key order also differs
    (the capture puts `model` first).
  - The capture thinking `content_block_start` carries `"signature":""`.
    `thinking_then_text.txt` does not.
  - Ids (`msg_01`, `tu_a`), model `claude-sonnet-4-6` and the signature
    `abc123` are placeholders.
- `error` event shape (`stream_error.txt`, `error_after_message_delta.txt`):
  no capture in the record has one. Write "not recorded" for its source.
- The four SMA-531 files (`eof_after_message_delta.txt`,
  `body_cut_inside_message_stop.txt`, `eof_mid_content_block.txt`,
  `error_after_message_delta.txt`) are cut or extended copies of
  `text_only.txt`. Their headers say so, and name `stream_error.txt` as the
  source of the `error` event in `error_after_message_delta.txt`. They point
  to the `text_only.txt` header for the shape comparison and do not repeat it.
- `tool_use_then_continuation.txt`: the header says that the file holds two
  separate response bodies and that `# --- turn 2 ---` is a test delimiter,
  not wire bytes.

### D4. Gemini `parallel_signed.sse`

Sven does not know whether the probe output was edited beyond the signature.
The header says:

- CAPTURED from the Gemini Developer API, streamed, `gemini-3.8-flash`,
  2026-11-20, SMA-827 (PR #373), capture 1 (three parallel calls). The exact
  URL is not recorded.
- Changed: the real 1140-character `thoughtSignature` is replaced with `SIG_A`.
- Removed and Added: not recorded.
- Two signs are unexplained: the JSON spacing is not consistent, and
  `candidatesTokenCount` rises in equal steps (14, 28, 42, 42). The header
  states them, so a reader does not read the values as proof of wire behaviour.
- The stream ends at EOF with no `[DONE]`. This matches the other Gemini
  capture (`conformance.rs`, Live capture section).
- It is a different capture from the `conformance.rs` capture
  (`gemini-3.6-flash`, 2026-08-20). Do not cite one as the source of the other.

### D5. LiteLLM fixtures

| File | Label | Header content |
|---|---|---|
| `text_then_trailing_usage.txt` | CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts | Capture: LiteLLM 1.97.0, `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`, digest `sha256:468c25f35f3e5ec4e414974f00deab93337b1b4d9953cabcfd3722e59415f834`, keyless `mock_response`, model `mock-fast`, SMA-451 (PR #199). Date: not recorded. Source: SMA-451 spec Appendix B (P1 trace). Captured: the finish chunk, the usage chunk and `[DONE]`. Reconstructed: the content deltas ("Hel", "lo"; the mock text was "Hello from the mock backend."). Changed: the id is a placeholder (`chatcmpl-1`). `created`: not recorded in the trace. |
| `truncated_no_finish.txt` | HAND-AUTHORED | Envelope from `text_then_trailing_usage.txt`. Ends with no finish chunk and no `[DONE]` on purpose (premature end). |
| `unknown_finish_reason.txt` | HAND-AUTHORED | Envelope from `text_then_trailing_usage.txt`. The value `guardrail_intervened` has no recorded source. The `[DONE]` matches the captured LiteLLM framing. |
| `unparseable_frame.txt` | HAND-AUTHORED | Synthetic by design. The line `data: {this is not json` is not wire bytes. |
| `tool_call_stream.txt` | CAPTURED (keep the header) | Add the edit list. The SMA-547 spec ("Evidence", "Captured frames") records only the `tool_calls` arrays. They match the fixture. Removed, Added and Changed for the `tool_calls` arrays: nothing (checked against the spec). For the rest of each chunk: not recorded. LiteLLM's key reorder and the added `"type":"function"` are proxy output, not edits (spec lines 129-131). |
| `tool_call_stream_fragmented_name.txt` | CAPTURED (keep the header) | The same as `tool_call_stream.txt`. |

The builder confirms each claim against the cited spec lines before writing it.

### D6. OpenAI Chat fixtures

| File | Header change |
|---|---|
| `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt` | Relabel as CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts. Proxy: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable` (digest and version: not recorded), keyless mock, 2026-08-16, SMA-522 (PR #197). Reconstructed: the ten content deltas. Edits: Removed: not recorded (the trace is abridged). Added: nothing beyond the reconstructed deltas. Changed: the id is shortened from `chatcmpl-1cc5e8c0-f16f-4180-a7f4-d14ba54837d7` to `chatcmpl-1cc5e8c0`. |
| `chat_text_usage_trailing_empty_choices.txt` | HAND-AUTHORED. Name the source of each shape: the envelope and `[DONE]` from `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`; `"choices":[]` from the async-openai field doc (quote it, as today). |
| `chat_content_filter.txt` | HAND-AUTHORED. Name the source of each shape. Record that SMA-522 (commit `b495a404`) split the usage chunk out of the finish chunk. State that the usage chunk keeps the LiteLLM-proxy form `choices:[{"index":0,"delta":{}}]`, not the first-party `choices:[]`. The `content_filter` value has no capture. |
| `chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt` | The same as `chat_content_filter.txt`. The tool-call delta shape: name the source if the record shows one, else "not recorded". |

### D7. Tools fixtures

- `brave_search.json`: a `///` doc comment on `parses_brave_fixture`
  (`src/web/backends/brave.rs`). HAND-AUTHORED under SMA-412 (PR #76). The
  shape is the subset that the SMA-412 spec (lines 307-310) maps:
  `web.results[].{title,url,description}`. Content is invented. No capture and
  no vendor doc link is recorded. The real response has more fields; their
  absence here does not mean absence on the wire. `parse_brave_respects_limit`
  gets a one-line doc comment that points to `parses_brave_fixture`.
- `tavily_search.json`: the same on `parses_tavily_fixture`
  (`src/web/backends/tavily.rs`), spec lines 312-318.
- `article.html`: not a provider wire fixture (it is extractor input). No
  header. The PR body says so.

### D8. CLI fixtures

`agents.toml`, `tools/lookup_spending.rhai`, `triage.jsonl` and
`triage_script.json` are not wire-format fixtures. They are config, a tool
script, an eval dataset and the SDK's own script format
(`crates/paigasus-helikon-evals/src/script.rs`). No header. The PR body says
so, because the ticket counts them.

### D9. Conformance suite (`tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs`)

The module-level "Fixture provenance" sections stay the main provenance layer.
Each helper doc comment already cites a fixture. The work is:

1. Each module "Fixture provenance" section gives the label of each source it
   cites (CAPTURED, HAND-AUTHORED, or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts),
   as the fixture headers now state it.
2. `openai_chat`: remove the claim "shapes OpenAI is actually observed to
   send". State that each source is a LiteLLM-proxy capture or a hand-authored
   file, and that no `api.openai.com` Chat capture exists.
3. Each helper that changes its source records the change in its doc comment,
   in one line. Known items:
   - `openai_chat::text_delta` adds `"finish_reason":null` (source: `chat_wire.rs`).
   - The `text_delta` helpers drop `"role":"assistant"` from the first delta.
   - The `usage_chunk` helpers drop `completion_tokens_details`.
   - `openai_responses` sets `sequence_number: 0` on every frame.
   - `gemini::tool_call_chunk` drops `index`, `role`, `modelVersion` and
     `responseId`, and trims `usageMetadata`.
   - The id and model constants are already disclosed. Do not repeat them.
4. `bedrock`: add the label HAND-AUTHORED (from the vendored
   `aws-sdk-bedrockruntime` types) to the module doc. State that the numeric
   values (11/4/15, `latencyMs` 314) are arbitrary. State that the order
   "metadata after messageStop" and "a real stream closes every block" have no
   capture.
5. `gemini::done`: add the words "synthetic, not captured".
6. `anthropic`: update the module doc so that it labels its sources
   HAND-AUTHORED, to match the new fixture headers.

### D10. Provider integration-test wire helpers (scope option 2)

Each helper and inline literal below that serves response bytes over HTTP gets
a doc comment (or a `//` comment on a literal) with its label and source. Most
are HAND-AUTHORED. Name the fixture or capture whose shape each one copies, or
write "not recorded".

| File | Items |
|---|---|
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/messages_wire.rs` | `empty_stream_response()`; the error bodies (529, 400, 401 and the fourth) |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/prompt_caching.rs` | `turn()` |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/structured_output.rs` | `synth_tool_use_stream()` |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/tests/gemini_wire.rs` | `sse_ok()` |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/tests/gemini_streaming.rs` | the inline `data:` bodies (about 5) |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/litellm_wire.rs` | `sse_ok()`; inline bodies (about 4) |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/streaming.rs` | the inline body near line 54 |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/cancellation.rs` | the `[DONE]` body |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/src/sse.rs` (test module) | the raw JSON chunk strings (about 4) |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/chat_wire.rs` | the SSE body (relabel the informal "Captured from LiteLLM"); the 429 error body |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/chat_streaming.rs` | the inline body near line 225 |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/cancellation.rs` | the `[DONE]` body; the inline body near line 98 |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/responses_wire.rs` | `text_delta_event`, `completed_event`, `sse` |
| `crates/paigasus-helikon/tests/openai_litellm_message_parity.rs` | the SSE body near line 147 |

The line numbers come from an inventory and are approximate. The builder finds
each item again before editing. Bodies that are not provider bytes
(`paigasus-helikon-tools/tests/web_fetch.rs` plain-text and HTML bodies) are
out of scope.

## Data changes

The scope allows a data change only for a line that the wire did not send.
The research found no such line in the in-scope files except these, which are
synthetic on purpose and get a header note instead of a change:

- `tool_use_then_continuation.txt`: the `# --- turn 2 ---` delimiter.
- `unparseable_frame.txt`: the bad JSON line.
- `body_cut_inside_message_stop.txt`: the cut final event.

If the builder finds another line that the wire did not send, record it in the
header. Do not remove it without a check with Sven.

## Verification

- `cargo test` for each touched crate and for
  `tests/provider-stream-conformance`, then
  `cargo test --workspace --all-features` once at the end.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and
  `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- `npx markdownlint-cli2` (for `CONTRIBUTING.md` and this spec).
- `git diff` shows no change below the header of any fixture file, except
  where a data change is recorded above.

## Left to the builder

- The exact wording of each header, within D1-D10.
- The order of the commits, one commit per crate or per fixture group.

Linear: [SMA-845](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-845/audit-wire-format-fixture-headers-in-other-crates-against-the-new).
Rule: `CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format fixtures" (added by SMA-585, PR #381).

## Intent

SMA-585 added a provenance rule for wire-format fixtures and made the OpenAI
Responses fixtures obey it. The fixtures and wire helpers in the other crates
do not obey it yet. A reader of those files cannot tell which bytes a provider
really sent. This change makes each in-scope fixture and wire helper state its
provenance under the rule.

## Goals

1. Each in-scope fixture file carries a provenance header that obeys rules 1-5.
2. Each in-scope JSON fixture has its provenance in the doc comment of the test
   that loads it (rule 5).
3. Each in-scope inline wire helper cites its source in its doc comment (rule 5).
4. Each statement in a header is true to the record. Where the record is silent,
   the header says so.

## Non-goals

- No new captures. This work uses only the record that exists today.
- No change to translator or production code.
- No change to the `#[cfg(test)]` unit tests that feed `json!` values or typed
  chunks into a translator (for example `litellm/src/stream.rs`,
  `gemini/src/stream.rs`, `openai/src/backend/chat.rs`,
  `bedrock/src/stream.rs`). These do not serve bytes over HTTP. Sven chose
  this scope (option 2) on 2026-11-21.
- No change to the SMA-840 branch. Its capture headers also do not obey the
  rule. That is a finding for SMA-840, not work for this branch.
- No mdBook or crate README change. This is test-only and contributor-doc work
  with no effect on the public surface.

## Anti-goals

- A header that says "nothing" for a part that nobody can check. That is the
  defect SMA-585 found, in a new form.
- A header that names a source (a doc page, a capture) that the record does not
  show was used.
- A data edit made only to make a fixture look like a sibling (rule 4).

## Constraints

- **Header syntax.** SSE and `.txt` fixtures use `:` comment lines.
  `eventsource-stream` 0.2.3 ignores comment lines (`event_stream.rs:70`), and
  a following blank line dispatches nothing (`:100`). The Gemini
  `translate/mod.rs:355-358` loop skips lines that do not start with `data: `.
  The LiteLLM and OpenAI fixtures that already have a `:` header pass their
  tests today. So a `:` header is safe in each SSE fixture.
- **`tool_use_then_continuation.txt`.** `messages_streaming.rs:201-203`
  splits the file on `# --- turn 2 ---\n` and asserts two parts. The header
  goes at the top (into part 1) and must not contain that delimiter string.
- **`body_cut_inside_message_stop.txt`.** The file ends inside an event with no
  newline, on purpose. The header goes at the top. Do not touch the tail.
- **Line endings.** `.gitattributes` pins these fixture directories to
  `text eol=lf`. Do not change that.
- **Merge order.** The Anthropic headers cite the SMA-840 captures. SMA-840 is
  not merged (local branch
  `feature/sma-840-anthropic-provider-drops-thinking-signatures`, no PR on
  2026-11-21). This PR must merge after SMA-840. Before the merge, check the
  cited SMA-840 files again on `main`.
- **Commits.** Use `test(providers)`, `test(tools)`, `docs(contributing)` and
  `docs(specs)`/`docs(plan)`. No `feat` or `fix`. Each touched crate still gets
  a release-plz patch bump, because the changed files are in packaged crates.
  That is accepted.

1. **One PR now, merged after SMA-840 (chosen).** All work is done now. The
   SMA-840 captures are read with read-only `git show` on that branch. The PR
   body states the merge order. Cost: a merge-order dependency.
2. **Two PRs.** Everything except the Anthropic headers merges now. The
   Anthropic headers follow after SMA-840 merges. No dependency, but two review
   loops.
3. **Wait for SMA-840.** Simple, but it stops all the work for one fixture

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

The Paigasus AI SDK (codename **Helikon**, after Mt Helicon where Pegasus's hoof struck the Hippocrene spring). A Rust SDK for building AI agents. All crates live under the `paigasus-helikon-*` namespace.

The full architectural reference lives in Notion: ["Crate Reference"](https://www.notion.so/355830e8fbaa813c92e8c1aa9985fd3f). Linear project: `Paigasus Helikon` (issues prefixed `SMA-`).

## Common commands

```bash
cargo build --workspace                              # all 14 crates
cargo build --workspace --all-features               # facade with every optional crate
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin helikon
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin paigasus-helikon
```

To reproduce **every** CI gate locally (matches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job-for-job):

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=80 NIGHTLY_CHANNEL=nightly-2026-05-01 \
  bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh                 # requires: rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-05-01
npm ci                                               # once, or after package-lock.json changes
npx markdownlint-cli2                                # reads .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc
bash scripts/check-markdownlint-config.sh            # asserts that config is in force
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh         # cargo-visible workflow env is uniform
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh # …and its parser still parses (fmt runs both)
bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh            # release gap report + release-plz.yml guards (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade-selftest.sh      # the cascade guard keeps its rule (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh                 # breaking bump needs breaking dependents (PR only; fmt runs it)
```

The full list lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (single source of truth for contributor policies).

## Workspace layout

15 crates under `crates/`. The facade `paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` unconditionally and the other 12 sibling crates behind Cargo features.

Every crate carries a real implementation and publishes to crates.io; zero name-claim stubs remain (first published in SMA-385, last ascends in SMA-333). One standing exception: `paigasus-helikon-cli` publishes as a **binary** crate — its lib target is internal (`missing_docs` opted out), carries no stability guarantee, and exists only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves. `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` publishes as a normal library crate (SMA-805); the three session backends keep a path-only dev-dependency on it. Exact versions move every release — read each crate's `Cargo.toml`, don't trust numbers written here.

Workspace inheritance is **mandatory**: per-crate `Cargo.toml`s only set `name`, `description`, and any crate-specific bits. Everything else (`edition`, `rust-version`, `authors`, `license`, `repository`, `homepage`, `keywords`, `categories`) inherits from `[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Don't hardcode these per-crate.

**Per-crate version is the one exception.** No stubs remain, so the 4-step ascend recipe is now historical — but two caveats still bite any PR that hand-bumps a version:

- **If a crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too**, along with its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and CHANGELOG. `cargo publish --verify` builds the tarball against the **registry** core, so otherwise the publish fails and release-plz deadlocks.
- **Any PR that hand-bumps a sibling must ALSO bump the facade** (`crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` version + its self-pin + CHANGELOG). release-plz does not bump the facade for a sibling version that is already at target when the PR merges, so a manual bump silently leaves the facade advertising stale dep reqs. (`dependencies_update = true` only makes the release PR run `cargo update` on `Cargo.lock`; it does not cascade version bumps.)
- **A breaking bump of a crate needs a breaking bump of each crate that depends on it.** release-plz gives a dependent without its own commits only a patch bump (release-plz#1599), and users then get two copies of the crate. The `fmt` job runs `scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh` to enforce this. See `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md` → "A breaking change in a crate with dependents".
- Feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.

Full lifecycle, the 4-step recipe, and the SMA-321/SMA-346 postmortems: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.

Third-party version pins live in `[workspace.dependencies]` (root). Members reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Internal crate paths are also in `[workspace.dependencies]` so the facade can use `workspace = true` consistently.

## Non-obvious patterns to preserve

- **Feature naming**: kebab-case in `[features]` (`runtime-tokio`), snake-case in `pub use` aliases (`runtime_tokio`). They must stay paired across the facade's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli` uses `autobins = false`** because the `paigasus-helikon` (hyphen) binary maps to `src/bin/paigasus_helikon.rs` (underscore — hyphens are illegal in Rust filenames). Removing `autobins = false` reintroduces a phantom `paigasus_helikon` binary that conflicts with the explicit `[[bin]]` entry.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate from day one** (`[lib] proc-macro = true`). Don't convert it to a regular lib even though it currently has no macros.
- **The `paigasus-helikon` facade lib shares its name with the `paigasus-helikon` CLI binary by design** (Notion ref's "fully-qualified shim alias"). This produces a non-fatal `cargo doc` filename-collision warning. Don't "fix" it by renaming either — both names are user-facing API. The accepted future fix is `doc = false` on the CLI binary entry.
- **License is dual `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`** (decided 2026-05-20, reversing the 2026-05-16 MIT-only call). Both `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` live at the repo root; the workspace metadata is `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"`. Per Rust ecosystem convention — no Apache-only or MIT-only crates in the workspace. Contributions are accepted under the same dual license by default (the standard inbound-equals-outbound clause is restated in `README.md`).
- **MSRV is `1.94`** (workspace-package level; raised from 1.85 in SMA-329 because sqlx 0.9.0 declares `rust-version = "1.94.0"` — the pre-existing highest floor in the workspace). If a dep raises MSRV, bump `rust-version` to what cargo demands rather than downgrading the dep.
- **Workspace-wide `missing_docs` enforcement** lives in root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.rust] missing_docs = "warn"`). Each non-CLI crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. The CLI overrides locally with `[lints.rust] missing_docs = "allow"` and does **not** include `workspace = true` — cargo treats `[lints] workspace = true` and an inline `[lints.<tool>]` table as mutually exclusive. When adding a new crate, copy the opt-in block. When adding a new `pub use` re-export to the facade, give it a `///` doc comment or `-D warnings` will fail the docs job.
- **`cargo msrv` has no `--workspace` flag.** The msrv workflow verifies one representative inheriting crate: `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify`. Because every member uses `rust-version.workspace = true`, success on one is success on all. Don't "fix" the workflow by adding `--workspace`; that's what the first SMA-305 CI run died on.
- **Nightly is date-pinned** (`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN: nightly-2026-05-01` at the workflow `env:` level in `ci.yml`, threaded into the doc-coverage script as `NIGHTLY_CHANNEL`). The rustdoc JSON coverage format is `-Z unstable-options` and can shift between nightlies; floating `nightly` would be a CI footgun. Bumping is a one-line follow-up chore, not an emergency.
- **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure must use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)` types**, never `feat`/`fix`. release-plz parses every commit since the last per-crate tag — a `feat(workspace): ...` commit that touches every `Cargo.toml` would attribute a bump to every crate. The SMA-307 bootstrap PR followed this rule; the same rule applies to any future `release-plz.toml` or `release-plz.yml` edits.

## Model routing

The general tiering rules are in the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Only the repo-specific rules are here.

- **Use Opus for release work.** This covers release-plz, the stub-ascend recipe, a hand-bumped crate version, and any red required gate. A wrong answer breaks a publish; see `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.
- **Haiku can read CI output.** Change to Opus when the question becomes *why* a required gate is red.

## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
